quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Computer user support specialists provide technical assistance to computer users, answering questions and resolving computer problems.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Computer User Support Specialists) include IT Support Specialist, Help Desk Analyst, Desktop Support Technician and Computer Support Specialist.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Three (medium preparation needed): most occupations in this zone require training in vocational schools, related on-the-job experience, or an associate's degree.

sections.heading: What an IT support specialist does
paragraphs: Computer user support specialists provide technical assistance to computer users, answering questions and resolving computer problems.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Computer User Support Specialists. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Answer users' questions about how software or hardware works.
Read manuals, talk to users and run diagnostics to investigate and resolve problems.
Set up equipment for employees, including cables, operating systems and software.
Install and make minor repairs to hardware, software and peripherals.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Three (medium preparation needed): most occupations in this zone require training in vocational schools, related on-the-job experience, or an associate's degree.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: BCA (Bachelor of Computer Applications); Certificate in Computer Applications.
Less common routes on the map: Polytechnic Diploma (Engineering); B.Sc (Bachelor of Science).
